title: Time and Signs
english: The sun and moon increase and decrease. Let them be for signs, and for seasons, and for days, and for years. The sun and moon produce this time. For the orbits, being ordered, generate the exits in a measured way. Time is called this, because as if on a circle, it is taken in orderly succession, first to second, and third to the next. And let them be for signs, because they always indicate the presence of winter; for mist, generated by the air, darkens the sun's rays, and appears coal-black and smoky, unable to disperse the air condensed from the vapors of the earth; and from this, a sign of winter is shown. When the so-called halos (some are circular figures similar to halos, from which they are so named) surround the sun, it indicates the severity of the winds; and when the so-called anthelions join in the sun's movement, it becomes a sign of aerial symptoms; and again, when rods-like things appear in the color of Iris in the morning among the clouds, it indicates rain, or winter, or a change in the air. The moon, when on the third day, is thin and clear in its horns, announces a stable calm; but if it is thick in its horns, and appears reddish, it announces abundant water or a violent south wind. Therefore, the sun and moon are the instruments of time; time is of days, months, and years; and the stars, of months, of sowing, and of harvest. And the Pleiades, rising in the time of the harvest, setting in the time of sowing, indicate this. And with the Wagon, they become a sign for sailors; for the stars become signs and markers of places. The Bear indeed shows the Bear It has only the day, as the psalmist also declares to us: 'He set the sun in authority over the day, the moon, and the stars in authority over the night.'
